title: Learn The Big Apple, Pt2 - for Lindy Hop and Swing Dance

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher provides a detailed, analytical breakdown of specific dance steps by comparing them to historical footage. She encourages students to develop their own personal style while acknowledging the foundational movements.

lesson_structure.note: The teacher introduces the lesson as part 2 of the Big Apple.
The teacher performs the full routine to music.
The teacher lists and demonstrates the specific moves used in the routine.
The teacher leads the student through the routine with counts.
The teacher discusses the importance of individual style in Lindy Hop.
The teacher analyzes specific steps by comparing her own performance to historical footage.
The teacher performs the routine at a faster tempo.

cues: kick ball change on count eight
common_mistakes: jumping with the right leg back instead of the left

what_works: The teacher uses side-by-side comparisons with historical footage to clarify complex movements.
The teacher clearly labels each step before demonstrating it.
what_hinders: The fast pace of the routine may be challenging for beginners to follow without frequent pausing.

quotes.text: I wanted to start with part two because, honestly, I think it's a little bit harder.
The tricky thing about Lindy Hop is that individual style is so important.
Ultimately, you draw your own line, which can shift and change as you learn.
No one has ever brought this up to me or told me I was wrong.
To me, thinking like that helps keep the footwork straight.

evidence_segments.observation: The teacher performs a series of rhythmic steps including swivels and kicks.
The teacher demonstrates the routine while counting aloud.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher uses historical footage to analyze and critique her own performance, highlighting discrepancies between her interpretation and the original choreography.
